title: Quantum enhancement and Doppler suppression of Kasevich-Chu atom interferometer with motional squeezing states
authors: Dongyang Yu, Yubin Wang, Fong En Oon, Qiang Lin
abstract: Hybridization of internal and external atomic degrees of freedom in a Kasevich-Chu interferometer enables the possibility to enhance the sensitivity significantly even under quantum-standard limit. By introducing motional squeezing state as an input, we systematically derive the computational framework of quantum and classical Fisher information of two measurement protocols for arbitrary strength of Doppler effects. Through maximizing the corresponding classical Fisher information, we obtain the optimal control parameters and the corresponding quantum Fisher information. For population measurement, the largest sensitivity can be as large as four times than the semi-classical limit through enlarging the atom coherence length. For joint measurement of population and position, the competition between quantum enhancement and Doppler suppression induces two three behaviors, in one regime, the quantum enhancement dominates even in presence of strong Doppler broadening effects where the sensitivity is significantly enhanced; while in another regime, an optimal squeezing parameter is observed where the classical Fisher information reaches the maximum. Our results clearly demonstrate the robustness of external quantum enhancement against Doppler suppression. Our proposal can be readily applied to gravimeter of mobile platform where decoherence from noise will damage the many-body entanglement of internal spin squeezing.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes Kasevich-Chu atom interferometers using motional squeezing states to boost measurement sensitivity. It rigorously compares performance under ideal conditions versus realistic Doppler broadening effects by calculating both Quantum and Classical Fisher Information for different measurement types. The key finding is that joint measurement of population and position provides a robust enhancement mechanism capable of overcoming significant Doppler suppression.
main_problem: The study aims to enhance the sensitivity of Kasevich-Chu atom interferometers beyond the standard quantum limit while quantifying the detrimental effects of Doppler broadening.
main_result: Joint measurement of population and position shows superior robustness, allowing quantum enhancement to dominate even in the presence of strong Doppler broadening effects. For population measurement alone, enhancements up to four times the semi-classical limit were achieved.
method: The authors systematically derived computational frameworks for both Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and classical Fisher information (CFI) by analyzing two distinct measurement protocols: population measurement and joint population–position measurement.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Kasevich-Chu atom gravimeter utilizing cold atomic ensembles. The theoretical model incorporates the hybridization of internal and external atomic degrees of freedom, allowing for the use of Motional Squeezing States (MSS) as input states.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information ($F_Q$) and Classical Fisher Information ($F_C$), sensitivity ($\delta g$), contrast ($C$).
important_parameters: Squeezing strength ($ eta$), squeezing angle ($	heta$), interrogation time ratio ($r=T_1/T$), Doppler effect magnitude.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares 'Ideal' scenarios (neglecting Doppler effects) with 'Doppler' scenarios that incorporate momentum broadening. In some calculations, optimal control parameters from the ideal case were adopted for the Doppler calculation due to numerical complexity.
figures_summary: Figures compare maximum CFIs/QFIs across different measurement protocols and squeezing parameters ($ eta, 	heta$) in both Ideal and Doppler regimes, highlighting the superior performance of joint measurements.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the theoretical framework using QFI/CFI for ideal vs. Doppler scenarios (using MSS input). It then optimizes control parameters to maximize CFI for population vs. joint measurement protocols, concluding with a comparative analysis showing robustness in the joint measurement regime.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes quantum metrology into regimes where real-world noise sources like Doppler shifts are present, providing concrete guidance on how entanglement resources (MSS) can maintain high precision measurements.
